restrictions: The two messages have 60 and 62 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length; the 62-byte message ends in two zero bytes.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every choice of nine state words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, and a second exact construction enumerates such pairs with the round-1 state word Y4 held inside a class of 4,096 values. Heuristic part: a search over 2^116 such pairs, all with Y4 in the class, for one whose remaining 128 digest bits agree.

Classical 256-bit word RAM with 64 registers (55 used; 32-register schedule also priced at 112.07). Seven trials in 36-bit lanes. Proof Section 11 uses two's-complement propagation in K3/D1 (~S15 = ~S11 + kc, d = ~S11 + X11 - X12 + 1) to cut batch ALU/control ops from 154 to 151 and eliminate constant '1', and pins all 42 batch constants in registers across the 586 batches of each alpha. Counted batch: 151 ALU/control operations plus 2 list loads (U[j], V[j]) plus 2 list-address additions, total 155. Per-alpha setup charged 512 (including 42 preload loads), giving 586*155+512 = 91,342 operations per alpha (22.3003 operations/trial exact -> 2^111.7945, or 22.5 operations/trial rounded -> 2^111.8068, both below 2^111.81). The early-pass cap remains 2^104, charged 4096 primitives each (2^116 total). Ready for organizer execution and review.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1 and H2. The factor 2,048 in H1 is assumed and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments; with the uniform rate instead, the same search needs 2^127 trials and gives time_log2 123.4. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed.

Six 32-bit constants and the 32-bit word eta that defines the class are stored in the program (28 bytes of advice); they were selected by participant measurements, the constants as the best of 4,140 candidate sets and the class among the classes seen in the samples, and recomputing the constants and selecting them and eta is bounded by 2^63 units and included in the time. No priority or novelty claim is made; the number of trials is 2^116 instead of 2^128 because a trial is assumed to succeed 2,048 times more often than a uniform 128-bit value would.

This package derives from Jbenisek (04638ed8, 112.4) and 5kyguy (c85fc92, 112.12), with credit also to tekkac (2bf40fb); all three are credited as originators and co-authors in that sense. Sections 1-10 reproduce the source argument and empirical reports as attributed material. Section 11 defines the complement-propagated 151-op batch and 64-register full-resident cost schedule (111.81). The declared organizer-executed experiments verify the 128-bit half-collision, 136-bit class residual search, and shared-seed S5-fixed early-test and schedule audit at finite scale; full 128-bit residual rate (H1) and full-run tail (H2) remain disclosed heuristic extrapolations.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the 2^116 enumerated trials behave with respect to the event that the 128-bit residual R is zero like independent events of probability at least 2^-117 each (2,048 times the rate of a uniform 128-bit value), to the extent that the probability that no trial has R = 0 is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.002.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 6.4: lengths 60 and 62, the six constants of Section 3.2, the class of Y4 defined by eta = e96d6d6b (Lemma Q), contexts indexed by (X12, X13, X14) with X12 < 2^8, the D0 family with parameter alpha, and all 4,096 members of the class for every context and alpha.
heuristics.extrapolation: From a participant estimate of the class rate, that is of the number of solutions with Y4 in the class of the seven-word system that determines R, obtained by sampling one of the two calls involved and counting the other call for each sample: a lower bound of 7,319 times the uniform expectation with standard error 816, from 2^41 draws for each of three values of an auxiliary difference, drawn with a new seed after the constants, the class and those three values were fixed. The count per sample is exact where the enumeration fits a work budget and a random-subset estimate otherwise. In that run 5,388 samples were counted: all 417 nonzero values are counts made in full, and the random-subset branch was used only for 915 samples, each with the estimate zero, of which 80 drawn at random were confirmed to have no solution by a SAT solver. Of the 417 nonzero counts, 100 were given to an independent model counter, which counted all of them: for the 40 largest, which carry 45.6% of the sum, the ratio of sums is 1.027, and for 60 drawn at random it is 0.969. The preceding pass of the same size, in which this class was the largest of eight and which is therefore biased upwards, gave 7,173 with standard error 778. Eight further passes of the same size with fresh seeds, after the same choices, gave sums between 5,946 and 7,785, with mean 7,003 and a standard error of the mean of 241. From checks of the counting program against an independent model counter on a run of 2^40 uniform samples (not samples of the class): for its random-subset branch the ratio of sums is 0.986 on the 40 largest estimates and 1.050 on 100 random nonzero estimates, and 100 of 100 random zero estimates are unsatisfiable; for its outcomes counted in full the ratio is 1.005 on the 40 largest and 1.000 on 60 random ones. From a repetition of the unrestricted estimate on another machine with another seed (13.5 with standard error 3.7 from 2^39 samples, against 10.6 with standard error 1.3), which supports the count under the model and not the class rate. From comparisons of the seven-word model with real trials of the class search at 32 bits on events of probability about 2^-32 and above: 2^42 real trials with an independent random context per thread against 2^42 model draws (early-test passes 5,498 against 5,463; largest deviation 1.5 standard deviations), and eight runs of 2^37 real trials with seed words shared by all contexts of a run (1,319 early-test passes in all, against 1,366 for the model figure scaled to the same number of trials; two statistics 2.3 and 2.1 standard deviations from the model). And from scaled-down end-to-end runs of the same class search on the same construction with 8-bit and 10-bit words, in which the collisions found are compared with the exact prediction of the model (9,835 against 9,837.9 predicted at 8 bits, 693 against 664.6 at 10 bits; the same check for the search without the class restriction gave 1,813 against 1,807.2 over ten constant sets and 1,465 runs). All of this is in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these to the rate of R = 0 over 2^116 real trials.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 2,048 is assumed. It is set against a participant estimate, a lower bound of 7,319 with standard error 816, which the organizer-run experiments do not measure; the success bound needs a factor of at least 2,045. With factor 1 (the uniform rate) the claim would be 2^127 trials and time_log2 123.4. The class rate is a heavy-tailed quantity, a sum of counts of very different sizes with 84% of it from one auxiliary difference. Two smaller passes for this class scattered far more than their standard errors suggest (9,472 with standard error 4,793 from 10 nonzero values, then 2,404 with standard error 831 from 13); only the passes with 2^41 draws are relied on (the second, the third and eight further seeds, ten sums between 5,946 and 7,785), and the assumed 2,048 is 3.4 times below the eight-seed mean and 2.9 times below the smallest seed. The six constants (best of 4,140 candidate sets) and the class were selected by participant measurements of this kind, and the largest of many noisy estimates is biased upwards: the sums of the first and second passes carry that bias, and only the third-pass figure 7,319 and the eight further seeds were obtained on fresh draws after the constants, the class and its auxiliary differences were fixed. The counting program is the participant's, and so is every check of it. The 417 nonzero values behind the 7,319 are counts made in full; the independent counter confirmed 100 of them (the 40 largest and 60 drawn at random) and was not given the other 317. On uniform samples it was applied to 30 outcomes of a first check, and to 100 counts made in full and 240 random-subset outcomes of the 2^40-sample run. How often the random-subset branch was used in the other passes and for the other classes was not examined, and brute force confirms the program only for 8-bit words, where that branch cannot be reached. The repetition on another machine used the same counting program. The model that six of the seven words behave like independent uniform words over the trials is tested on real messages only for events of probability about 2^-32 and above, and end to end only at small word sizes (a scaled-down hash with 8-bit and 10-bit words); its use at 2^-117 cannot be tested directly. At 32 bits two statistics of the runs with shared seed words are 2.3 and 2.1 standard deviations from the model, and comparisons for two other classes and for the unrestricted search showed deviations of 2.6, 2.7 and 3.1. A second run of the unrestricted search showed the 3.1 again, in the same pair statistic, with the opposite sign: that is not a consistent bias, but a spread between runs larger than a Poisson count allows (larger in the model draws than in the real trials), which bears on the independence assumption and is under study. All trials of a run share the four seed words, trials of one context share most other words, and the 4,096 trials of one context and alpha differ only in Y4 and what follows from it; their independence is assumed. The main 32-bit comparison gave every context its own random words; the eight runs with shared seed words left one context word random that the algorithm sets to zero, so the state word S5 was not shared in them; and the scaled-down runs hold other words fixed than a run of the algorithm does. So the distribution of collisions within one run of the algorithm has not been tested directly; the scaled-down runs test it for another choice of the words held fixed. Organizer-executed experiments (`half-collision`, `residual-search`, `resident-audit`) verify the 128-bit half-collision, the 136-bit class residual search across 256 seeds, and low-nibble residual hits in the shared-seed S5-fixed layout at finite scale; the full 128-bit residual enhancement factor (2,048 at probability 2^-117) cannot be directly measured within sandbox limits and remains a disclosed heuristic extrapolation from the Section 10 model-counting and scaled-word evidence.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.999 over the random word, fewer than 2^104 of the 2^116 trials pass the 32-bit early test of proof.md Lemma E without having R = 0.
heuristics.scope: The early test of Section 6.3 on the trials of Section 6.4. The measured pass rate 2^-29.6 would give 2^86.4 passes; the budget of 2^104 corresponds to a pass rate of 2^-12 and is larger by a factor of about 2^17.6, and processing 2^104 passes is charged in the time bound (2^116 operations in the resident-mask derivative).
heuristics.extrapolation: From organizer-executed shared-seed S5-fixed batch audits in `resident-audit` (56 shared-seed S5-fixed trials per organizer seed across 256 seeds) and participant measurements of the pass rate on real trials of the class search at 32 bits (5,498 passes in 2^42 trials with an independent random context per thread; 1,319 passes in eight runs of 2^37 trials with seed words shared by all contexts of a run, between 150 and 177 per run; 2^42 draws of the seven-word model gave 5,463; all in proof.md Section 10) to the 2^116 trials of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Organizer-executed `resident-audit` verifies early-test equivalence and pass counts in the exact shared-seed S5-fixed layout at finite scale (56 trials per seed across 256 seeds), while the 2^42 independent-context and eight 2^37 shared-seed runs in Section 10 are participant-reported measurements. That the pass count of a full run of 2^116 trials stays below the 2^104 cap (which is 2^17.6 times larger than the expected 2^86.4 passes at rate 2^-29.6) is a heuristic tail extrapolation. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H2 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.001.
